critical_code_review_comments: routers/files.py::_may_access — correctly grants access to uploader (owner_id match), broadcast-scope files, and to sender OR recipient via db.notifications lookup on data.attachments.file_id + $or {user_id, data.sender_user_id}. Sender path is important since only the recipient's notification row exists; the query covers both.

routers/files.py::download_file — dual auth (Bearer via get_current_user then ?sid= via _user_from_sid) is correctly wired; _user_from_sid mirrors get_current_user's expiry handling (naive datetime → UTC coercion + expired-token None). Suspended-user block honoured. Cache-Control 'private, max-age=3600' prevents cross-user CDN caching — good.

services/capabilities.py — 11 capabilities defined; policies cover super_only/primary_only/owner_only/owner_implicit/owner_revocable/staff_default_true consistently. has_capability semantics preserved exactly for legacy require_* deps (owner_implicit == owner tier passthrough + flag; owner_revocable for blog uses can_create_blog is not False for owner tier; staff_default_true for personal messages allows non-patient staff unless explicit False). Confirmed at runtime: primary_owner gets all 10 non-platform-admin caps true.

app/messages/[id].tsx::AttachmentRow — Phase C dual-shape support is clean: initialises displayUri = data_url || null and, when data_url is absent, calls getAttachmentDisplayUri(att) to resolve the /api/files/{id}?sid=<token> URI for <Image> rendering. useEffect deps include data_url, att.file_id, att.url — correct.

routers/messaging.py::messages_send — MAX_ATTACHMENTS cap applied, attachments loop preserves both legacy (data_url/data_base64) and new (file_id/url) shapes when persisting into notification data.attachments (Mongo doc shows file_id+url only, no base64 bloat for new uploads).
